claims.text: The target material is an as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi high-entropy alloy in nanoscale thin-film or patterned-nanoribbon form.
Pulsed-laser-deposition-like methods can produce nanoscale alloy materials with controlled size and composition.
The proposed deposition route yields significant interfacial strain in FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons.
The proposed deposition route yields nanoscale compositional heterogeneity in FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons.
Strain-induced modulation of local magnetic anisotropy and magnetic coupling primarily governs the low-field magnetocaloric response and hysteresis.
Interfacial and size-confinement-induced chemical and structural inhomogeneities amplify the strain-mediated magnetic effect.
Nanoscale inhomogeneities alter phase stability and magnetic-domain dynamics relative to bulk FeMnNiGeSi.
Moderate post-deposition annealing under an inert atmosphere is the controlled intervention.
Moderate annealing will partially relax interfacial strain without causing significant grain growth or phase separation.
Moderate annealing will promote limited short-range chemical ordering or homogenization near interfaces.
Localized interfacial strain and variations in short-range chemical order affect magnetic-domain-wall dynamics and local magnetic anisotropy.
Interfacial strain and compositional inhomogeneity pin magnetic domains and create magnetic energy barriers.
Domain pinning and associated energy barriers cause larger hysteresis.
Domain pinning and associated energy barriers smear or broaden the magnetocaloric response.
Annealing-induced strain relaxation and interfacial ordering will reduce domain-wall pinning.
Annealed samples will exhibit a sharper magnetocaloric response than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit a moderately increased peak magnetocaloric effect under low applied field.
Annealed samples will exhibit a smaller hysteresis-loop area than the as-deposited baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies near room temperature at field amplitudes below approximately 100–200 mT in the nanoscale regime.
Nanoscale heat-transfer limitations may interact with magnetic-domain dynamics during cycling.
